analyst_view.overall: Marseille are 4th and have won five Ligue 1 games in a row under Bruno Genesio (2-1 at Lens last time out), while promoted Le Mans are 15th with 8 points and one win in their last six (1-1 with Monaco before the break). Marseille are without left-back Emerson (knee operation) and defender Derek Cornelius (hip, out until the end of the year); Le Mans miss attacking midfielder Adil Bourabaa (ankle surgery) and right-back Djibril Sidibé (broken foot), with Samuel Yohou a doubt after a head knock. None of these absences is on the numbers' missing list, but all have been out for weeks, so recent form already reflects most of them. Marseille host Levski Sofia in the Europa League on Thursday 26 November, so some rotation or game management is possible, and the upper Virage Sud will be closed after an LFP sanction. No referee was named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, 2.6 of them Marseille's, already boosted a little for their 14 goals in the last six. I lean slightly lower to about 3.5: Emerson's absence takes away an attacking left-back, and with Levski Sofia coming on Thursday Genesio may rotate or ease off once ahead. Le Mans' missing creator Bourabaa has been out since October, so that is mostly in their form already.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.1 corners and already take a little off for both sides' low corner counts lately (Le Mans won 18 in six against 24 expected). Emerson's absence could mean fewer overlaps on the left, but Marseille should still have most of the ball against a side near the bottom, so nothing clearly points either way and I stay at about 8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, with more expected from Le Mans, who have picked up 16 cards in their last six and are usually chasing the ball in games like this; the numbers already count that form. No referee has been named yet, and it is not a derby or a heated fixture, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 26 shots, about 15 for Marseille and 11 for Le Mans. Marseille's winning run and Le Mans' struggles are in the form figures already, and the possible rotation before the Europa League game is too uncertain to size, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target and already trim Marseille's for their recent 24 in six (30 expected). Gouiri remains Marseille's main scorer and no new absence hits either attack beyond what has been out for weeks, so I stay at about 9.
